item.title: Pointwise Riesz potential bounds for rough singular integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.31888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a complete characterization of the kernels $\Omega\in \Lup^1(\Sp)$ for which the rough singular integral $\T_\Omega$ and the associated maximal operator $\M_\Omega$ satisfy pointwise bounds by $\Int_1(|\nabla \cdot|)$ and $\M_1(|\nabla \cdot|)$, respectively, where $\Int_1$ is the Riesz potential and $\M_1$ is the fractional maximal operator. These bounds hold if and only if $\Omega$ belongs to the homogeneous dual Sobolev space $\dot \W^{-1,\infty}(\Sp)$. Equivalently, $\Omega=\text{div}_\Sp \mathbf{V}$ for some bounded vector field $\mathbf{V}$ on the sphere, or $\big|\int_E\Omega\big|\leq C\,\mathcal H^{d-2}(\partial E)$ for every open set $E\subseteq\Sp$ with smooth boundary. On the Lebesgue scale, we show that for $d\geq3$ the condition $\Omega\in\Lup^{d-1,\infty}(\Sp)$, together with mean zero, suffices, and that the exponent $d-1$ is sharp. Finally, in dimension $d=2$, we use complex-analytic methods to prove a new pointwise bound in terms of the complex derivative $\bar\partial f$ that is valid for every mean-zero $\Omega\in\Lup^1(\mathbb S^1)$. As a consequence, we obtain new Sobolev bounds for rough singular integrals in the plane.
item.dc:creator: Kabe Moen, Carlos P\'erez

item.title: Sobolev Orthogonal Polynomials on the unit circle with varying inner product
item.description: arXiv:2610.31994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the validity of the Szeg\"o type strong asymptotic formula for the Sobolev orthogonal polynomials associated with a Sobolev-type inner product depending on a parameter $s$, which is defined as \begin{equation*} \langle f,g\rangle _{\frac{\lambda}{n^s}}:= \int_{\mathbb{T}} f(z)\overline{g(z)} d\mu_1(z)+ \dfrac{\lambda}{n^s} \int_{\mathbb{T}} f^{\prime}(z)\overline{g^{\prime}(z)} d\mu_2(z), \quad \text{where $s$ is fixed and } \quad s\geq 2, \end{equation*} and $\lambda >0$. Here, $\mu_1$, $\mu_2$ are absolutely continuous with respect to the normalized lebesgue measure and $\int_{\mathbb{T}} \mu^{\prime}_i(z) dm=1$, where $\mu_i^{\prime}(z)= \dfrac{d\mu_i}{dm} >0$ for $i=1,2$. Further, $\mu_1, \mu_2$ belongs to the Szeg\"o class and also has non-zero bounded Radon-Nikodym derivatives on the unit circle. %satisfies $ 0 <m \leq \dfrac{\mu^{\prime}_1(e^{\iota \theta})}{\mu^{\prime}_2(e^{\iota \theta})}\leq M < \infty $. We observe that the measure appearing in the Szeg\"o function of the strong asymptotic limit depends on $s$. As a specific case, we consider the Bernstein-Christoffel Sobolev orthogonal polynomials and study their properties, including the asymptotic distribution and location of their zeros for different values of $s$. We further establish a spectral characterization of their zeros as the eigenvalue of an explicitly constructed modification of the associated Hessenberg matrix and provide numerical evidence supporting the obtained asymptotic and zeros results.
item.dc:creator: Sourav Majumder, A. Swaminathan

item.title: Pinned configuration sets and slicing theorems via Fourier integral operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.32088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_X}$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_Y}$ be open, where $d_X,d_Y\geq2$ and $1\leq p\leq\min\{d_X,d_Y\}$. Let $\Phi:X\times Y\to\mathbb R^p$ be a smooth mapping, and suppose that $D_x\Phi$ and $D_y\Phi$ have rank $p$. For compact sets $A\subset X$ and $B\subset Y$, we give lower bounds on $\dim_H A+\dim_H B$ ensuring that the pinned configuration set \[\Delta_\Phi^y(A)=\{\Phi(x,y):x\in A\}\] has positive Lebesgue measure or nonempty interior for some $y\in B$. The dimensional thresholds are expressed in terms of uniform $L^2$-Sobolev estimates for the generalized Radon transforms associated with $\Phi$. Our results extend the Fourier integral operator approach developed by Greenleaf, Iosevich, and Taylor for unpinned $2$-point configuration problems to the pinned setting. We also prove a nonlinear projection theorem that remains valid even when the Peres-Schlag transversality condition fails. Under the smoothing hypotheses used for the pinned configuration theorem, we obtain lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimensions of the corresponding slices of $A$ by the level sets of $\Phi$. Applications include distances from points to hyperplanes, spheres and lines; multiparameter distance sets; and a restricted projection family introduced by Harris.
item.dc:creator: Allan Greenleaf, Eyvindur Ari Palsson, Minh-Quy Pham, Giorgos Psaromiligkos

item.title: Coefficient duality and interpolation of Euclidean flag Besov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to develop the duality theory of the homogeneous Besov spaces associated with the Euclidean flag, using the discrete Littlewood--Paley--Stein analysis. We first establish an exact discrete sampling formula together with bounded analysis and synthesis maps, by which the space is identified with a sequence space of coefficients. The continuous dual is then computed through a coefficient norm. In this computation the geometry of the sampling rectangles plays an essential role: when the spatial exponent is below one, the volume of a dyadic rectangle forces an explicit shift of both smoothness indices. We devote particular attention to the supremum sequence exponent. At that endpoint the closure of the flag test functions is characterized by vanishing scale tails, and the limiting tail is comparable to the distance to this closure; every continuous functional on the full space decomposes into a canonical regular part and a part that annihilates the closure, and the latter may be nonzero. For finite exponents the dual is again a flag Besov space. As applications, finite Calder\'on sums give a quantitative approximation theorem, and the common analysis and synthesis framework yields real and complex interpolation as well as the lifting property. The arguments are based on the exact sampling formula, scalar maximal estimates and the transpose of one bounded coefficient projection.
item.dc:creator: Chang Li

item.title: Weak-$L^\infty$ and BMO with Hausdorff Content
item.description: arXiv:2610.32231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ on measure space was introduced by Bennett et al. (Ann. of Math., 113(1981), 601-611) and proved to contain the space of $L^\infty$ and possess the appropriate interpolation property. In this paper, we are aimed to continue this line of research on the Euclidean space $\mathbb R^n$ endowed with Hausdorff content, which is a low-dimensional outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and fails to be additive or absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measures. But low-dimensional subsets, such as fractals, of $\mathbb{R}^n$ are Hausdorff capacitable. Precisely, in the setting of Hausdorff content, an analogue of weak-$L^\infty$ is defined and proved to possess an improved Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem. Moreover, we show that the space of functions with bounded mean oscillation associated to the Hausdorff content is embedded into this new weak-$L^\infty$ space by establishing a key estimate for the distribution via a packing condition. As a by-product, the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood operator on the space of weak-$L^{\infty}$ is established.
item.dc:creator: Hao Guo, Long Huang, Yangzhi Zhang, Ciqiang Zhuo

item.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $\mu$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(\mu)$, then $\mu$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.
item.dc:creator: John Hoffman

item.title: Dimension-free bounds for maximal operators associated to log kernel and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.32641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M_\psi$ be the maximal operator associated to $\psi(x)=-\ln(1-|x|^2)$. We obtain dimension-free bounds on $L^p(\mathbb R^d)$ for $M_\psi$, $1<p\le\infty$. We show that the weak $L^1$ estimate does not hold for $M_\psi$, but does hold for the corresponding lacunary maximal operator $M_\psi^D$. An weak $L\log L$ type estimate for $M_\psi$ is obtained, which seems to be the right substitution for the weak $L^1$ estimate. Estimates for $M_\psi$ are applied to dimension-free estimates for maximal Riesz transforms obtained by Mateu, Verdera, Orobitg and P\'{e}rez.
item.dc:creator: Mingming Cao, Honghai Liu, Zengyan Si, Haibin Yan

item.title: Properties and applications of Muckenhoupt $A_1$ growth weights
item.description: arXiv:2610.32653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $\beta\ge0$, let $A_1^{(\beta)}$ be the class of weights satisfying $$ [w]_{A_1^{(\beta)}}:= \sup_{0<\varepsilon\le1} \varepsilon^\beta[w]_{A_{1+\varepsilon}}<\infty. $$ These classes satisfy $A_1\subsetneq A_1^{(\beta)}\subsetneq\bigcap_{p>1}A_p$ for $\beta>0$. For every $\alpha\ge0$, we prove that $w\in A_1^{(\beta)}$ if and only if $$ w\left(\left\{M_{L(\log L)^\alpha}f>\lambda\right\}\right) \le C\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{|f(x)|}{\lambda} \left[ \log\left(e+\frac{|f(x)|}{\lambda}\right) \right]^{\alpha+\beta} w(x)\,\mathrm{d}x. $$ The least constant $C$ is comparable to $[w]_{A_1^{(\beta)}}$. Also, we obtain corresponding characterizations for Calder\'on--Zygmund operators and their commutators.
item.dc:creator: Dinghuai Wang

item.title: Weighted decoupling inequalities via fractal bilinear Kakeya estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.32655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decoupling inequalities for the parabola are obtained for weights in physical space. The decoupling iteration relies on a fractal bilinear Kakeya estimate. We record applications to exponential sums.
item.dc:creator: Robert Schippa

item.title: Rational $S$-functions for second order ODEs with non-Liouvillian first integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.32769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $S$-function method for rational second order ODEs $y''=\varphi(x,y,y')$ uses $S=I_y/I_z$, attached to a first integral $I$, which satisfies a Riccati equation along the flow; it was designed for Liouvillian $I$. We study the case of rational $S$ with non-Liouvillian $I$. From any rational $g(x,y,z)$ with $g_z\neq0$ and any linear equation $A_2w''+A_1w'+A_0w=0$ with polynomial coefficients, the substitution $w'/w=g(x,y,y')$ yields a rational 2ODE whose first integral is built from two independent solutions, and $S=g_y/g_z$: the Wronskian cancels, so $S$ does not see the linear equation, and one rational $S$ is shared by equations with and without Liouvillian first integrals. Conversely, given $(\varphi,S)$, membership in this class reduces to a rational first integral of an explicit planar vector field plus a M\"obius-invariant Riccati test in $x$, which recovers the linear equation. A transfer theorem shows that $I$ is Liouvillian if and only if this equation has a Liouvillian solution, so Liouvillianity is decidable on the class by Kovacic's algorithm: a three-variable problem with no a priori degree bound is reduced to two classical ones. On nine pull-back equations of degree up to $15$, given without information on their construction, the procedure recovers the Airy equation and the Bessel equation of order zero.
item.dc:creator: L. G. S. Duarte, L. A. C. P. da Mota

item.title: Sharp Projection Bounds for Intermediate Dimensions of Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.32808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp bounds for the upper and lower intermediate dimensions of orthogonal and radial projections of compactly supported measures. Both dimension functions are preserved almost everywhere when the quasi-Assouad dimension does not exceed the target dimension. We obtain exceptional-set estimates using the entire source dimension function, with sharpness for explicit families. We also construct a fixed measure whose projected dimension functions vary on open direction sets, even when all source dimensions lie below the target dimension.
item.dc:creator: Shengyang Zang, Yingyu Zhao, Yunhao Zhao, Chen Zhou

item.title: Lacunary maximal operators on convex boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.32873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We disprove the cap-sufficiency proposal in Wright's Problem 16 for $1<p<(\sqrt{13}-1)/2$ and for $p>3$. For each fixed exponent in these ranges, one smooth strictly convex domain has finite original directional cap integral, while the lacunary maximal operator of complete arclength fails restricted weak type. We also give a geometric sufficient condition for strong $L^p$ boundedness, for every finite $1<p<\infty$, on an arbitrary given bounded convex domain. It requires one logarithmic integral of a curvature lower envelope, without a differentiability assumption on the boundary or a restriction on the number of curvature zeros. Both results concern unnormalised true arclength, one fixed interior origin and all integer dyadic dilations.
item.dc:creator: Xi Cen, Xinfeng Wu

item.title: A direct proof of the equivalence of the A2 and the Helson--Szego conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a direct proof of the equivalence between the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ and the Helson--Szeg\H{o} conditions on the unit circle $T$. A positive weight $w$ belongs to $\mathcal{A}_2(T)$ if and only if $\log w=u+Hv$, where $u,v$ are real bounded functions, $\|v\|_\infty<\frac{\pi}{2}$, and $H$ denotes the periodic Hilbert transform. The classical proof combines the Helson--Szeg\H{o} theorem with the Hunt--Muckenhoupt--Wheeden characterization of weighted boundedness of the Hilbert transform. Our proof derives the Helson--Szeg\H{o} representation directly from the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ condition, without using boundedness of $H$ on $L^2(w)$.
item.dc:creator: Christos Grigoriadis, Michail Paparizos, Georgios Psaromiligkos

item.title: Additive energy and Fourier complexity of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31807v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the additive energy and the Fourier approximation of graph adjacency matrices labeled by a cyclic group. For a graph with $N$ vertices, $s$ edges and adjacency matrix $M$, the additive energy of its directed edge set is at most $\min\{(2s)^3,N^2\operatorname{tr}(M^4)\}$, and equality in the spectral bound holds exactly when the labeling attains the graph-energy lower bound for the Fourier ratio. Such a labeling also minimizes every best $k$-term Fourier approximation error, whose square equals the tail of the squared adjacency singular values. We prove that graphs of odd prime-power order admit an equality-attaining labeling exactly when they are cyclic Cayley graphs, and a connected example on $15$ vertices shows that equality need not imply vertex transitivity at other orders. We construct regular graph families with asymptotically maximal normalized additive edge energy and unbounded minimum Fourier ratio, one of them with density tending to one half. For dense graph sequences under uniformly random labelings, the collision dimension differs from the reciprocal squared edge density by a quantity tending to zero in probability. We also prove a quantitative stability estimate for the graph-energy bound and show why its dependence on a spectral scale cannot be omitted, even for regular graphs. For a rank-$m$ orthogonal projector we prove $m\leq D_4\leq\operatorname{FR}^2$, characterize the equality $D_4=m$ by cyclic translation invariance, and obtain a quantitative approximation by a circulant projector.
item.dc:creator: Vishal Gupta, Sam Ferguson, Alex Iosevich, Joshua Iosevich, Haoyuan Tian, Ben Song

item.title: Displacement structure and eigenvalue bounds for multiband prolate matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.32082v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain explicit non-asymptotic bounds for the eigenvalue transition of multiband prolate matrices. Let $S\subset[-1/2,1/2]$ be a finite union of pairwise disjoint intervals, and let $\lambda_0\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_{N-1}$ be the eigenvalues of $B_{N,S}$. If $\nu$ is the number of boundary points of $S$ on the frequency torus, then, for every $0<\eps<1/2$, \[ \#\{k:\eps<\lambda_k<1-\eps\} \le \nu\ceil{\frac{\log(4N)}{\pi^2} \log\!\left(\frac{4}{\eps(1-\eps)}\right)}. \] Compared with the multiband estimate of Zhu and Wakin~\cite{wakin2017approximating}, this improves the dependence on $\eps$ from order $1/[\eps(1-\eps)]$ to logarithmic dependence. We also prove a second bound in which the main logarithmic term depends on the time--bandwidth product $N|S|$ rather than only on $N$. We also compare $S$ with frequency sets having fewer boundary points. Using a classical large-sieve estimate, we take into account not only the total size of the change in the frequency set, but also how that change is distributed. For sets with many small gaps, this can give a bound growing like $\log N$ for fixed $\eps$, even when the bounds based only on the total size of the gaps grow at least linearly in $N$. We also obtain exponential bounds for individual eigenvalues and use them to estimate the error in approximating sampled multiband signals by leading eigenvectors. A discretization argument gives corresponding results for the continuous problem. Numerical examples compare the bounds and examine how the locations of the frequency intervals affect the eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Luis Gomez, Hana Huber, Azita Mayeli

item.title: Gagliardo--Nirenberg extremals on manifolds with small holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.32173v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the sharp homogeneous Dirichlet Gagliardo--Nirenberg quotient on a closed Riemannian manifold with holes of small capacity and connected complements. For each fixed exponent $2<q<2^*$, the nonnegative $L^2$-normalized extremal exists and is unique when the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_D$ is sufficiently small. If the ambient volume is $V$ and $\beta=n(q-2)/2$, the sharp constant satisfies $C_D=V^{1-q/2}\lambda_D^{-\beta/2}(1+O(\lambda_D))$. For the normalized first eigenfunction $\varphi_D$, we obtain $\|u_D-\varphi_D\|_{H^1}=O(\lambda_D^{3/2})$ and $C_D/W_{M_D}(\varphi_D)=1+O(\lambda_D^2)$, together with a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the relative deficit. The constants depend only on the ambient manifold and the exponent. On general compact manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions, we prove compactness above the Euclidean sharp constant and describe concentration at equality. Positive scalar curvature at one interior point implies attainment. For the $L^2$-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger energy, the mass threshold for negative energy tends to zero as the capacity of the holes tends to zero, whereas the threshold for unboundedness below is unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Utsab Sarkar

item.title: Counterexamples for lacunary dilates via dyadic spike blocks
item.description: arXiv:2604.18535v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct counterexamples, along dyadic lacunary sequences, to two problems of Erd\H{o}s on the almost-everywhere behavior of sums $\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)$ on the circle. The main device is a dyadic spike block: rare positive spikes, each counted many times by a run of consecutive dilates, make the lacunary averages large, while a deterministic lower bound on every block prevents the rest of the series from cancelling them. We obtain a mean-zero $f\in\bigcap_{1\le q<\infty}L^q(\mathbb T)$ and a sequence $n_j=2^{m_j}$ with $n_{j+1}/n_j\ge2$ such that $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-1/2}$ and $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)=+\infty$ for almost every $x$. This answers negatively a question of Erd\H{o}s on whether the condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log\log N)^{-C}$ suffices for almost-everywhere convergence, and shows that Matsuyama's condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-c}$, $c>1/2$, cannot be relaxed to $c=1/2$. A second choice of parameters gives, for every $2\le p<\infty$, functions $f\in L^p(\mathbb T)$ with $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)/(N(\log N)^{1/p-\varepsilon})=+\infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, almost everywhere. This is sharp up to $\varepsilon$, and the case $p=2$ answers negatively a second question of Erd\H{o}s. Finally, a bounded variant in the spirit of Marstrand's disproof of Khintchine's conjecture gives sets of arbitrarily small measure whose lacunary visiting frequencies have limsup $1$ almost everywhere.
item.dc:creator: Boon Suan Ho

item.title: Weighted $H^p-L^q$ boundedness of integral operators with rough kernels
item.description: arXiv:2607.03567v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study integral operators \begin{equation*} T_\alpha f(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}K(x,y) f(y)dy, \end{equation*} with kernels $K(x,y)= k_1( x- A_1y)...k_m( x-A_my),$ where $k_i(x)=\frac{\Omega_i(x)}{|x|^{n/q_i}}$ and $\Omega_i: \mathbb{R}^n\to \mathbb{R}$ are homogeneous functions of degree zero, satisfying a size and a Dini condition, $A_{i}$ are certain invertible matrices, and $\frac n{q_1}+\dots+\frac n{q_m}=n-\alpha,$ $0\leq \alpha <n.$ We obtain the $H^{p}_{w^p}(\mathbb{R}^{n})-L^{q}_{w^q}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ boundedness of these operators, for a class of Muckenhoupt weights $w$, satisfying the condition \begin{equation*} w(A_ix)\leq cw(x), \end{equation*} $a.e.x\in\mathbb{R} ^n $, $1\leq i\leq m$.
item.dc:creator: Andrea L. Gallo, M. Silvina Riveros, Lucas A. Vallejos

item.title: Characterization of the boundedness of the segment multiplier on rearrangement-invariant spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.22277v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given rearrangement-invariant (r.i.) spaces $X$ and $Y$, we show that the segment multiplier, the truncated Hilbert transform, and the discrete Hilbert transform (on the associated discretized space) are bounded from $X$ to $Y$ simultaneously. Moreover, when $X = Y$ this boundedness is characterized by a condition on a pair of Boyd-type indices. We also exhibit an r.i. space on which the segment multiplier is bounded while the (non-truncated) Hilbert transform fails to be bounded.
item.dc:creator: Miguel F. Barea-Fern\'andez, Ron Kerman, Jan Lang, Javier Soria

item.title: Diagonal and branchwise criteria for universal Fourier series
item.description: arXiv:2610.27348v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize diagonal profiles admitting universal real trigonometric Fourier series with factors in $\mathcal E_s=\bigcap_{p>s}\ell^p$ and $\ell^{s,q}$, $2\le s<\infty$, $1\le q\le\infty$. For nonincreasing profiles we obtain exact dyadic criteria and logarithmic endpoints. For independently regular odd/even sine/cosine branches we characterize simultaneous subseries, sign, and rearrangement universality for finite almost-everywhere targets. One function in every $L^p$, $1\le p<2$, supplies the coefficients. A separation example admits this realization although every compatible nonincreasing majorant with bounded relative cost belongs to $\ell^1$. Residue-class decompositions extend the criterion; a weakest-model condition permits extended-real rearrangement targets. A Walsh--Paley counterpart yields the same diagonal multiplier thresholds for ternary $\{0,\pm1\}$-universality, together with a Fourier--Walsh realization. Trigonometric realization uses Pogosyan's majorant theorem; the multiplier, factorization, projection-transfer, separation, and Walsh Fourier-origin arguments are proved here.
item.dc:creator: Sergo A. Episkoposian

item.title: Hausdorff dimension of the graph of the unweighted error-sum function of continued fractions
item.description: arXiv:2507.16536v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the unweighted error-sum function $\mathcal{E}(x) \coloneqq \sum_{n \geq 0} (x - p_n(x)/q_n(x))$, where $p_n(x)/q_n(x)$ denotes the $n$th convergent of the continued fraction expansion of $x \in \mathbb{R}$, and we prove that the graph of $\mathcal{E}$ has Hausdorff dimension $1$. The key ingredient is an exact formula for the oscillation of $\mathcal{E}$ on fundamental intervals, which we obtain in a symbolic space of continued fraction sequences containing non-realizable sequences. Using the same framework, we also give a new derivation of the upper bound $3/2$ of Ridley and Petruska (2000) for the Hausdorff dimension of the graph of the relative error-sum function $P(x) \coloneqq \sum_{n \geq 0} (q_n(x)x - p_n(x))$. Moreover, we present an alternative argument based on M\"obius inversion and summation over coprime convergent denominators, and we explain why the square coverings used for $P$ cannot yield an upper bound smaller than $3/2$.
item.dc:creator: Min Woong Ahn

item.title: The Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $p<1$
item.description: arXiv:2508.13243v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $0<p<1$, thereby extending earlier constructions for $1\leq p\leq \infty$. We then establish various properties of these spaces, including their behavior under complex interpolation and duality, and their invariance under Fourier integral operators. We also obtain Sobolev embeddings, equivalent characterizations, and a molecular decomposition. These spaces are used in the companion article arXiv:2502.02511 to determine the sharp $\mathcal{H}^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ and $\mathrm{bmo}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ regularity of wave equations with rough coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Naijia Liu, Jan Rozendaal, Liang Song

item.title: A H\"ormander spectral multiplier theorem for fractional Hardy operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.31532v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the fractional Laplacian with added critical or subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator. We prove a H\"ormander spectral multiplier theorem, i.e., the boundedness of sufficiently smooth multipliers of these Hardy operators on Lebesgue spaces. The range of admissible Lebesgue exponents is optimal, but the smoothness assumption is probably not. The proof combines the Helffer--Sj\"ostrand formula with a quantitative Jaffard lemma for operator-valued matrices.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Merz
